title: Technology Sector Update for 08/21/2018: DGLY,FN,GSB,HPE
text:

MSFT -0.80%
AAPL -0.30%

CSCO -0.95%
GOOG -0.50%
Technology stocks gave back almost all of their prior gains, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding just over 0.1% in value during late trade although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index continues to roar higher with a more than 1.9% rise.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Digital Ally ( DGLY ) advanced during Tuesday trading, at one point rising over 8%, after the digital video and storage company closed on an additional $9.5 million in new funding from Brickell Key Investments LP, increasing proceeds from the two-step financial package to $10 million. The company expects to use the proceeds to repay and retire the $5.5 million in senior secured convertible promissory notes it issued on April 4, with the remaining funds to be used to cover other general corporate costs, including litigation expenses.
In other sector news:
+ GlobalSCAPE ( GSB ) rose as much as 14% on Tuesday after the software developer announced plans for a modified Dutch auction tender offer seeking to repurchase up to $15 million of its common shares at between $4 to $4.50 each, or a premium of up to 29.7% over GlobalSCAPE's closing price on Monday. The tender offer is expected to begin over the next few days and remain open for the next 20 business days.
+ Fabrinet ( FN ) touched an 18-month high on Tuesday, rising over 9% to reach its best share price since February 2017 at $48.05 a share, after reporting above-consensus financial results for its fiscal Q4. Excluding one-time items, the optical packaging company earned $0.81 per share during the three months ended June 29 on $345.3 million in revenue, exceeding Street views by $0.06 per share and $7.2 million, respectively. It also sees adjusted Q1 earnings in a range of $0.80 to $0.83 per share, topping the Capital IQ consensus by at least $0.01 per share. Despite the upbeat financial results and forecast, however, analysts at Needham & Co lowered their stock rating for Fabrinet shares to Buy from Strong Buy previously.
- Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) was almost 5% lower this afternoon after analysts at Bernstein cut their investment recommendation for the software company's stock to Market Perform from Outperform.
